{{ElectionsOH}}
The '''1994 United States Senate election in Ohio''' took place on November 8, 1994. Incumbent Democratic U.S. Senator [[Howard Metzenbaum]] decided to retire after 19 years in the [[United States Senate]]. Republican nominee [[Mike DeWine]] won the open seat against Democratic nominee Joel Hyatt, Metzenbaum's son-in-law. Independent candidate, conservative [[anti-abortion]] activist Joe Slovenec performed very well, getting over 7% of the vote. DeWine was the first Republican to win a U.S. Senate race in Ohio since [[1970 United States Senate election in Ohio|1970]].

== Democratic primary ==
=== Candidates ===
* Ralph A. Applegate, Columbus businessman<ref name=latimes>{{cite news|title=Race to Succeed Metzenbaum Is Down to Wire|date=May 4, 1994|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|location=Columbus, Ohio|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1994-05-04-mn-53586-story.html}}</ref>
* [[Mary O. Boyle]], Cuyahoga County Commissioner and former State Representative from [[Cleveland Heights, Ohio|Cleveland Heights]]<ref name=latimes/>
* [[Joel Hyatt]], attorney, businessman and son-in-law of incumbent U.S. Senator [[Howard Metzenbaum]]

== General election ==
=== Candidates ===
* [[Mike DeWine]], [[Lieutenant Governor of Ohio|Lieutenant Governor]] and nominee for Senate in [[1992 United States Senate election in Ohio|1992]] (Republican)
* [[Joel Hyatt]], businessman and son-in-law of incumbent U.S. Senator [[Howard Metzenbaum]] (Democratic)
* Joe Slovenec, [[anti-abortion]] activist<ref>{{Cite news |last1=Apple |first1=R. W. Jr. |date=15 September 1994 |title=THE 1994 CAMPAIGN: OHIO; TV Makes Ohio Candidate, then Turns and Hurts Him |url=https://www.nytimes.com/1994/09/15/us/the-1994-campaign-ohio-tv-makes-ohio-candidate-then-turns-and-hurts-him.html?pagewanted=2 |newspaper=The New York Times}}</ref> (Independent)
